one: Engineering methodology from LLM pipelines to compound AI systems to autonomous agents: choose the problem, decompose it, pick components, and evaluate.
pos: CS 329Z is one of the closest courses to the AI engineer role, taught by Diyi Yang and others. It emphasizes that an agent is not one model but a compound system of LLMs, retrievers, tools, and optimizers; students build RAG, tool use, and an agent loop from scratch, then move to frameworks such as DSPy.
topics: **Compound AI systems**: design patterns for multi-component systems
**Tool use**: function calling, tool selection, error handling
**Agent loop**: planning, execution, reflection, termination conditions
**DSPy**: declarative optimization of prompts and pipelines
**Data curation and evaluation**: building eval sets, offline/online metrics
**Three applied homework assignments + a quarter-long project**
prereq: Programming ability; LLM basics (prompting, API use); ML background is a plus.
assess: Three fully applied homework assignments plus a quarter-long project, focused on building, optimizing, and evaluating. Check the current syllabus for details.
who: Aspiring AI engineers/agent engineers; people moving from backend/ML to LLM applications; founders.
tips: It complements CS 224V: 224V is research/formal, 329Z is engineering/eval. Don't just get the demo running — make the evaluation solid.
